fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “If you see your brother’s ox or sheep straying, you must not ignore it; be sure to return it to your brother.” (Deuteronomy 22:1) No strolling past with a fake phone call. I spent years lost in the back of a junk drawer, so believe me, a neighbor who stops is a beautiful thing.

Sending him out of the city isn't part of this law, friend. The elders punish him and fine him a hundred shekels of silver, paid to the young woman's father (Deuteronomy 22:18-19). And she remains his wife. He must not divorce her as long as he lives.

Lying to the elders doesn't come up, friend. Moses gives this reason for the young woman: “…because she did not cry out in the city…” (Deuteronomy 22:24) The man is stoned for a different reason, because he has violated his neighbor's wife.

That's the reason, baker. Moses says both are stoned, “…the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he has violated his neighbor’s wife.” (Deuteronomy 22:24) This is a heavy one. Two people, two reasons, and Moses gives each reason plainly.
Her family isn't named in the reason, friend. Moses says she is stoned “…because she did not cry out in the city…” (Deuteronomy 22:24) That's the one reason he gives for her, and it's a heavy one.

Yes, baker. Moses says, “This case is just like one in which a man attacks his neighbor and murders him.” (Deuteronomy 22:26) He sets it right beside murder. The woman cried out, and the verse says there was no one to save her (Deuteronomy 22:27). This one is heavy.
Enemy isn't in the verse, friend. Moses says, “This case is just like one in which a man attacks his neighbor and murders him.” (Deuteronomy 22:26) The word he uses is neighbor.

That's right, baker. Along with the fifty shekels of silver, “…she must become his wife because he has violated her. He must not divorce her as long as he lives.” (Deuteronomy 22:29) Two requirements, and both are in that one verse.
